title: Fractions and decimals
part: Part I · The grammar of number
soi: The same quantity can be written as a fraction, a decimal or a measurement; choosing a representation makes comparison and calculation more reliable.
engage: A recipe must serve nine people instead of six. How can every ingredient change proportionally without changing the taste?
atl: In order for a student to transfer mathematical knowledge, students must connect representations and apply a known method in a new measurement or recipe context.
objectives: Use all four operations with fractions and decimals.
Round with stated precision and convert representations.
Scale a recipe and justify exact versus rounded measurements.
vocabulary: numerator · denominator · equivalent · simplest form · common denominator · reciprocal · terminating · repeating · precision

sections.title: Equivalent fractions and simplest form
sections.intent: Multiply or divide numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number.
paras: Fractions describe equal parts of one whole. 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 name the same amount when the wholes are the same size. The number of pieces changes, but the covered amount does not.
To simplify, divide top and bottom by a common factor. A fraction is in simplest form when its numerator and denominator have HCF 1.

example.title: Simplify 36/48
example.problem: Find a common factor, or divide by the HCF.

sections.warning: Equivalent fractions use the same whole. Half of a small pizza is not the same amount as half of a large pizza.

practice.prompt: Complete 2/3 = □/12.
A student changes 3/5 to 5/7 by adding 2 to both parts. Is it equivalent?
practice.answer: No. 3/5 = 0.6, while 5/7 ≈ 0.714. Multiply or divide both parts by the same nonzero number.
practice.reasoning: Adding equal amounts does not preserve a ratio.

practice.prompt: Write three fractions equivalent to 4/6, including its simplest form.
practice.reasoning: Simplify by 2, or scale both parts.

practice.prompt: A recipe uses 12 cups of flour out of 16 cups of dry ingredients. What fraction is flour, in simplest form?
A fraction simplifies to 3/5 and its denominator is 40. Find the numerator.

diagram.caption: Three equal wholes. The same amount is shaded in each bar.

sections.title: Comparing and ordering fractions
sections.intent: Use a common whole, a common denominator, a benchmark or a common numerator.
paras: With equal denominators, more parts means a larger fraction. With equal numerators, more parts means each part is smaller. For 3/7 and 3/5, fifths are larger than sevenths.
For unlike parts, use a common denominator: 3/4 = 9/12 and 5/6 = 10/12, so 5/6 is larger. A benchmark such as 1/2 can make comparison faster.
sections.warning: A larger denominator does not automatically mean a larger fraction. Always check the numerator and the size of the whole.

practice.prompt: Compare 3/7 and 3/5 using <, > or =.
practice.reasoning: Equal numerators: fifths are larger pieces than sevenths.

practice.prompt: Compare 3/4 and 5/6.
Order 2/3, 3/5 and 7/10 from smallest to largest.
Which is closer to 1: 7/8 or 8/9? Explain.
practice.answer: 8/9 is closer: its gap is 1/9, smaller than 1/8.
practice.reasoning: Compare the missing parts, not just the numerators.

practice.prompt: Amina reads 5/8 of a book and Ben reads 2/3 of an identical book. Who has read more?
practice.reasoning: The books are the same size, so the fractions can be compared.

practice.prompt: Find a fraction strictly between 1/3 and 1/2 with denominator 12.

verify.expr: [n for n in range(13) if F(1,3)<F(n,12)<F(1,2)]

sections.title: Adding and subtracting fractions
sections.intent: Make the parts the same size before combining or comparing amounts.
paras: For like denominators, add or subtract numerators and keep the denominator. For unlike denominators, first write equivalent fractions with a common denominator.
Mixed numbers can be handled as whole and fractional parts or as improper fractions. Borrowing one whole means borrowing denominator/denominator, not 1/10.
sections.warning: Do not add denominators: 1/2 + 1/3 is not 2/5. It must be more than 1/2.

practice.prompt: Calculate 3/8 + 1/8 and 7/9 − 2/9.
Calculate 3/4 + 5/6.
Calculate 5 1/3 − 2 3/4.
Explain why 1/2 + 1/3 cannot equal 2/5.
practice.answer: 2/5 is less than 1/2, but adding a positive amount to 1/2 must increase it. The correct sum is 5/6.
practice.reasoning: Use a benchmark to detect an unreasonable result.

practice.prompt: A jug contains 3/4 litre. Another 1/3 litre is added. How much is in the jug?
Find the missing addend: 2/5 + □ = 1 1/10.

sections.title: Multiplying and dividing fractions
sections.intent: Use “a fraction of” for multiplication and “how many groups?” for division.
paras: To multiply fractions, multiply numerators and denominators: a/b × c/d = ac/bd. An area model shows why: a rectangle split into b by d equal parts has ac shaded parts.
Dividing by a nonzero fraction asks how many of those fractional groups fit. Dividing by c/d is multiplying by d/c. For example, 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 6.

example.title: Find 2/3 of 3/5
example.problem: Use a rectangle split into thirds one way and fifths the other.

sections.warning: Multiplying by a proper fraction makes a positive amount smaller. Dividing by a proper fraction can make it larger.

practice.prompt: Calculate 2/3 × 3/5 and 4/7 × 7/8.
Calculate 3/4 ÷ 1/8 and 5/6 ÷ 5/3.
practice.reasoning: Multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor.

practice.prompt: A recipe needs 3/4 cup of milk. How much is needed for half a recipe?
How many 1/4-litre cups fill a 3/2-litre jug?
Explain why 6 ÷ 1/2 is 12, not 3.
practice.answer: There are two halves in each whole, so six wholes contain 12 halves.

practice.reasoning: First add to get 11/12, then multiply by 6/5.

sections.title: Decimal place value, ordering and rounding
sections.intent: Read place value, compare from left to right and round only at the requested stage.
paras: Digits right of the decimal point represent tenths, hundredths, thousandths and so on. Trailing zeros can record precision: 0.40 and 0.4 have equal value but different stated precision.
Compare equal place values from left to right. To round, inspect the next digit: 0–4 rounds down, 5–9 rounds up. Keep trailing zeros when they show the requested decimal places.

example.title: Round 0.995 to two decimal places
steps: The hundredths digit 9 rounds up and carries through the tenths digit.
Write two digits after the point.

sections.warning: 0.35 is larger than 0.4? Compare tenths first: 3 tenths is less than 4 tenths. Length in digits is not size.

practice.prompt: Write the value of the 7 in 3.072.
practice.reasoning: The first digit after the point is tenths; the second is hundredths.

practice.prompt: Order 0.35, 0.4, 0.305 and 0.45 from smallest to largest.
Calculate 3.7 + 0.48 and 5 − 2.36.
Calculate 0.6 × 0.4 and 2.4 ÷ 0.3.
practice.reasoning: 6×4 = 24 with two decimal places; 24 tenths ÷ 3 tenths.

practice.prompt: Round 0.995 to two decimal places and explain the zeros.
practice.answer: 1.00. The zeros show accuracy to two decimal places.
practice.reasoning: The 5 causes a carry through both 9s.

practice.prompt: A length is 4.7 cm to one decimal place. Give the interval of possible exact lengths under the usual half-up convention.
practice.reasoning: Values at 4.65 round up; 4.75 rounds to 4.8.

sections.title: Fractions, decimals and measurement
sections.intent: A fraction bar means division; choose the representation that makes the task clearer.
paras: To convert a fraction to a decimal, divide numerator by denominator, or rewrite with denominator 10, 100 or 1,000 when possible. 3/8 = 0.375.

A reduced fraction terminates exactly when its denominator has no prime factors except 2 and 5. Otherwise its decimal repeats: 1/3 = 0.333…. Use an exact fraction when a rounded decimal would hide the value.
sections.warning: A calculator display is often rounded. 0.333 is an approximation to 1/3, not exactly equal to it.

practice.prompt: Write 3/8, 7/20 and 2/5 as decimals.
Write 0.24 and 1.125 as fractions in simplest form.
Which of 3/8, 7/20 and 5/6 has a repeating decimal? Explain.
practice.answer: 5/6 repeats. Its reduced denominator contains a factor 3.

practice.prompt: Compare 3/8 inch and 0.4 inch. Which is larger and by how much?
One cup is defined here as 240 mL. How many mL are in 3/4 cup and 1 1/2 cups?
Calculate 0.75 + 2/5 − 0.3 exactly.

diagram.caption: A common scale makes 3/8 = 0.375 and 0.4 directly comparable.

explore.title: Which fractions stop?
explore.instruction: Criterion B. Test reduced fractions, record patterns and justify a rule using prime factors.
explore.intro: A terminating decimal ends after finitely many digits. A repeating decimal continues a repeating block forever.

items.prompt: Convert 3/8, 7/20, 5/6 and 7/15 to decimals. Identify which terminate.
items.reasoning: Divide numerator by denominator and mark repetition.

items.prompt: Factor the denominators 8, 20, 6 and 15.
items.reasoning: Prime factors explain the stopping behaviour.

items.prompt: State the rule for a fraction already in simplest form.
items.answer: It terminates exactly when its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5.

items.prompt: Predict whether 13/40 and 13/30 terminate, then check.
Why must the fraction be reduced before applying the denominator rule? Give an example.
items.answer: A non-reduced denominator may hide a cancelling factor. 3/6 = 1/2 terminates even though 6 contains 3.
items.reasoning: The rule concerns the reduced denominator.

application.title: The scaling kitchen
application.instruction: Criterion D. Simulated recipe. In this task, 1 cup = 240 mL. Keep exact amounts until the final measurement.
application.intro: A community kitchen scales a recipe for different group sizes. The original recipe serves 6 people and uses 3/4 cup milk, 1 1/2 cups rice and 2/3 cup oil.

items.prompt: Scale the recipe to 9 people. Give each ingredient in cups.
items.answer: Milk 9/8 = 1 1/8 cups; rice 9/4 = 2 1/4 cups; oil 1 cup.

items.prompt: Convert the 9-person milk and oil amounts to mL.
A cook adds the scale factors for two ingredients instead of multiplying each amount. Explain the error.
items.answer: Each ingredient must be multiplied by the same scale factor 3/2. Adding 3/2 changes the amount by a fixed quantity, not proportionally.

items.prompt: For 4 people, the cook has 100 mL milk. Is it enough? Find the surplus or shortage.
items.answer: Not enough. The recipe needs 1/2 cup = 120 mL, so 100 mL is 20 mL short.

assessment.title: The measurement explainer
assessment.instruction: Criteria A and C. Use a diagram, exact fractions and a clear comparison for a workshop card.
assessment.intro: A fitting is labelled 3/8 inch; another is labelled 0.4 inch. A learner must choose the larger without rounding too early.

items.prompt: Convert 3/8 inch to a decimal and compare with 0.4 inch.
Calculate 2/3 + 1/4 and explain a diagram that checks the result.
items.answer: 11/12. A 3-by-4 rectangle has 8 shaded columns for 2/3 and 3 more rows for 1/4, covering 11 of 12 cells.
items.reasoning: A common denominator makes parts equal.

items.prompt: Write one misconception warning and one check question with its answer.
items.answer: Sample warning: “Do not add denominators.” Check: 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4, not 2/6.
items.reasoning: The answer should expose the error and show a correct alternative.
